# kaneo_project

Manages a Kaneo project within a workspace. Deleting a project permanently deletes its tasks and other contents.

## Example usage

```terraform
# Replace with an existing workspace ID.
resource "kaneo_project" "platform" {
  workspace_id = "existing-workspace-id"
  name         = "Platform"
  slug         = "PLAT"
  icon         = "Code"
  description  = "Platform engineering tasks"
  is_public    = false
}
```

<!-- schema generated by tfplugindocs -->
## Schema

### Required

- `name` (String) Project name. Must not be empty.
- `slug` (String) Prefix used in task identifiers, for example `PLAT` in `PLAT-12`. Must not be empty.
- `workspace_id` (String) Workspace identifier. Changing this replaces the project rather than moving it and deletes its old contents without copying them.

### Optional

- `description` (String) Project description. Defaults to an empty string. Removing this argument clears the description.
- `icon` (String) Project icon name. Defaults to Layout.
- `is_public` (Boolean) Whether the project board is readable without signing in. Defaults to false.

### Read-Only

- `archived_at` (String) Project archive timestamp, or null if not archived. This resource reads archived projects but does not manage archiving or sidebar order.
- `created_at` (String) Project creation timestamp.
- `id` (String) Project identifier.

Null API descriptions become empty strings; null visibility becomes `false`. Description or visibility setup can fail after creation; refresh and review the plan before retrying.

## Import

```shell
terraform import kaneo_project.platform project-id
```

Import retrieves the workspace ID and project attributes. Match them before applying. See the [import guide](https://registry.terraform.io/providers/glitchedmob/kaneo/latest/docs/guides/import) for declarative imports and dependency guidance.

New projects get four [default columns](https://registry.terraform.io/providers/glitchedmob/kaneo/latest/docs/resources/column#import-and-default-columns); import those rather than creating duplicates.
